data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's four-case taxonomy claims exhaustiveness but fails the problem's 'determine exactly when' standard because it does not cover the case where exhaustion truncates exactly at a framing-boundary marker that is itself corrupted. This is neither pure case C (ambiguous framing of data) nor pure case D (corruption detected in record content) — it is a boundary-integrity failure that bridges both. Since the target asserts these four cases are exhaustive, any unclassified truncation scenario leaves a gap in both the permissibility and refusal rules, meaning the target cannot 'determine exactly when' for that scenario.
